statement: Keep at least 80% of weekly running time in zone 1 (at or below LT1/VT1) as the default, and never plan below 70%.
appliesTo: All distance runners, 5 km to marathon; also the default for ultra

statement: Default shape is pyramidal (zone 1 > zone 2 > zone 3). Prior of about 80/12/8 time in zone 1/2/3 with a tolerance of +/-5 percentage points on each zone; treat as a prior, not an optimum.
appliesTo: Recreational and sub-elite runners in base and build phases

statement: Never plan a threshold-dominant week or block (zone 2 time greater than zone 1 time); cap zone 2 at about 12% of time in base phases and at about 25% in any phase. Threshold sessions remain allowed inside these caps.
For goals up to the marathon, keep zone 3 at roughly 5-10% of time in build and specific phases (about 8% default); do not remove high-intensity work entirely. Exact optimum is unknown.
appliesTo: Runners training for 5 km to marathon who tolerate high-intensity work

statement: Choose TID type by athlete level: recreational runners get pyramidal; polarized is permitted only for competitive athletes, in blocks shorter than 12 weeks aimed at VO2max or short-event performance. Treat polarized and pyramidal as equivalent for time-trial performance.

For 5-10 km goals in well-trained runners, run pyramidal in the base/early build and shift to polarized in the later specific block, holding total load constant across the switch. Reference design: 8 weeks pyramidal then 8 weeks polarized.
appliesTo: Well-trained (competitive) runners with 5-10 km goal; not validated for marathon or ultra

statement: For marathon and longer goals keep the pyramidal shape through the specific phase and let race-pace work rise as the race approaches (race-pace share grows, total low-intensity share stays at or above the floor).

No TID trial exists for ultra or 100-mile runners. Use a conservative default of at least 85% zone 1 time, zone 3 kept small (about 5% or less), and long time-on-feet sessions; set race-day pacing below LT1/VT1 for most of the event.

Compute and store TID by time-in-zone and by session goal; label every displayed percentage with its method. Session-count and time-based percentages are not interchangeable (skier conversion: factor 0.9 for zone 1 and 3.0 for zones 2-3 from time to session goal; not validated for runners).
appliesTo: All plans and all TID displays

statement: Report TID against both physiological anchors (LT1/LT2 or HR/pace proxies) and goal-race-pace anchors, and name the anchor whenever the plan is labelled pyramidal or polarized.
appliesTo: All plans; race-specific sessions defined by goal pace

statement: When HR or pace data are missing, derive session intensity zone from session RPE and use it to count TID; use more than one method when both are available.
appliesTo: Athletes without usable HR or pace data

statement: Show executed versus planned TID to the athlete and flag easy runs executed above zone 1. The 5 percentage point flag threshold has no direct evidence and is a conservative engine default.
appliesTo: Recreational runners with HR or pace data

statement: Separate hard days with easy days; no consecutive hard days by default. The recommendation is from elite-runner reviews; applying it to recreational runners is a conservative inference.
appliesTo: All runners; evidence is from highly trained and elite runners

statement: For runners with few sessions per week, plan the TID budget in minutes, not sessions: compute the weekly zone 2+3 time allowance (about 20% of time, no more than 25%) and size quality sessions to fit. An 80/20 split by session count overstates hard time share.
appliesTo: Recreational runners with 3-5 runs per week

statement: Treat all TID targets as priors with an uncertainty band and expose the plan's TID type as a descriptive output, not an optimization objective; do not present polarized or pyramidal as proven superior.
appliesTo: Plan generator design and user-facing copy
